annotation.targetText: The family no longer produces; it only consumes. The housework that remains consists of cleaning, cooking, washing, and mending. annotations.chapterTitle: 3. Property Rights in Marriage and Female Inequality

annotation.summary: Examining demographic imbalances between men and women caused by war, emigration, industrial accidents, and economic crises, Bebel refutes those who tell women that marriage is their sole 'natural profession' when millions of women are structurally prevented from marrying.
annotation.explanation: Examining demographic imbalances between men and women caused by war, emigration, industrial accidents, and economic crises, Bebel refutes those who tell women that marriage is their sole 'natural profession' when millions of women are structurally prevented from marrying.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XI: The Chances of Matrimony

annotation.targetText: Marriage constitutes one phase of the sex relations of bourgeois society; prostitution constitutes the other.
annotation.summary: Bebel demonstrates that prostitution is not an isolated moral failing, but a necessary social institution of bourgeois society, forming the shadowy complement to pecuniary bourgeois marriage and driven directly by female poverty, low wages, and patriarchal double standards.
annotation.explanation: Bebel demonstrates that prostitution is not an isolated moral failing, but a necessary social institution of bourgeois society, forming the shadowy complement to pecuniary bourgeois marriage and driven directly by female poverty, low wages, and patriarchal double standards.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XII: Prostitution a Necessary Social Institution of Bourgeois Society

annotation.targetText: The endeavor of women to earn their own living and to attain personal independence is, to some extent at least, regarded as a just one by bourgeois society.
annotation.summary: Tracking the rapid influx of women into capitalist factories, sweatshops, and industrial trades, Bebel shows how machinery allows capitalists to replace male workers with lower-paid women and children, subjecting working women to intense exploitation while laying the material basis for their collective organization.
annotation.explanation: Tracking the rapid influx of women into capitalist factories, sweatshops, and industrial trades, Bebel shows how machinery allows capitalists to replace male workers with lower-paid women and children, subjecting working women to intense exploitation while laying the material basis for their collective organization.

annotation.targetText: Although the change in the position of women is obvious to all who go through life with open eyes, we still continue to hear the idle talk that the home and the family are woman's natural sphere.
annotation.summary: Bebel chronicles women's struggle for higher education and entry into the professions (medicine, science, teaching, administration), alongside how industrial capitalism itself revolutionizes domestic life by replacing household production with commercial food processing and appliances.
annotation.explanation: Bebel chronicles women's struggle for higher education and entry into the professions (medicine, science, teaching, administration), alongside how industrial capitalism itself revolutionizes domestic life by replacing household production with commercial food processing and appliances.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XIV: The Struggle of Women for Education

annotation.targetText: The social dependence of a race, class, or sex, always finds expression in the laws and political conditions of the country in question.
annotation.summary: Reviewing the discriminatory civil and political laws of European states, Bebel shows how legal codes reflect ruling-class and patriarchal interests, and explains why working-class women join forces with Social Democracy to win universal suffrage and civic equality.
annotation.explanation: Reviewing the discriminatory civil and political laws of European states, Bebel shows how legal codes reflect ruling-class and patriarchal interests, and explains why working-class women join forces with Social Democracy to win universal suffrage and civic equality.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XV: The Legal Status of Women

annotation.targetText: This chapter may be brief. It merely contains the conclusions that may be drawn in regard to the position of woman in future society, from all that has been said so far; conclusions that every reader can easily draw for himself.
annotation.summary: Summarizing woman's position in future socialist society, Bebel declares that woman will be socially and economically independent, no longer subjected to any trace of domination or exploitation, free to choose her partner solely on the basis of mutual love and respect.
annotation.explanation: Summarizing woman's position in future socialist society, Bebel declares that woman will be socially and economically independent, no longer subjected to any trace of domination or exploitation, free to choose her partner solely on the basis of mutual love and respect.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XXVIII: Woman in the Future

annotation.targetText: If it were a matter of bourgeois ladies voting, the capitalist state could expect nothing but effective support for the reaction. Most of those bourgeois women who act like lionesses in the struggle against "male prerogatives" would trot like docile lambs in the camp of conservative and clerical reaction if they had suffrage.
annotation.summary: Luxemburg exposes how upper-class feminists fight for male privileges within their class, but eagerly vote for conservative, anti-labor, and reactionary policies once granted the franchise.
annotation.explanation: Luxemburg exposes how upper-class feminists fight for male privileges within their class, but eagerly vote for conservative, anti-labor, and reactionary policies once granted the franchise.

annotation.targetText:
Does it require deep intuition to comprehend that man's ideas, views,
and conception, in one word, man's consciousness, changes with every change
in the conditions of his material existence, in his social relations and
in his social life?

What else does the history of ideas prove, than that intellectual
production changes its character in proportion as material production is
changed? The ruling ideas of each age have ever been the ideas of its ruling
class.
annotation.summary: Refutation of philosophical idealism: human consciousness and ruling ideas are shaped by material production and class power.
annotation.explanation: Against idealist philosophers who claim that eternal ideas drive history, Marx and Engels demonstrate that ideas evolve alongside material social relations, and that the dominant ideology of any epoch reflects the material interests of its ruling class.

annotation.targetText: The scientific significance of N.I. Bukharin's work consists particularly in this, that he examines the fundamental facts of world economy relating to imperialism as a whole, as a definite stage in the growth of most highly developed capitalism.
annotation.summary: Lenin highlights that imperialism must be analyzed scientifically as a definite historical stage of highly developed monopoly capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Rather than treating imperialism as a reversible diplomatic policy choice or a moral insult, Marxism analyzes it as the necessary economic stage reached when free competition gives way to monopoly.

annotation.targetText: The cleavage between "town and country," as well as the "development of this cleavage," formerly confined to one country only, are now being reproduced on a tremendously enlarged basis. Viewed from this standpoint, entire countries appear to-day as "towns," namely, the industrial countries, whereas entire agrarian territories appear to be "country."
annotation.summary: World capitalism reproduces the division between town and country on a global scale, turning industrial powers into 'towns' and agrarian colonies into 'country'.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin extends Marx's analysis of the urban-rural division of labor to the world economy, explaining how uneven capitalist development polarizes the globe into industrial manufacturing centers and dependent agricultural or extractive peripheries.

annotation.targetText: The fact is that the very foundation of modern states as definite political entities was caused by economic needs and requirements. The state grew on the economic foundation; it was only an expression of economic connections; state ties appeared only as an expression of economic ties.
annotation.summary: Contrary to idealist theories of the 'state principle', modern nation-states emerged as political expressions of underlying capitalist economic ties.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin applies historical materialism to refute bourgeois state idealism, demonstrating that the national state arose to consolidate and protect the economic connections of the national bourgeoisie.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. IV: The Inner Structure of "National Economies" and the Tariff Policy

annotation.targetText: Marxism teaches us that the historic process, and consequently every link in the chain of historic events, is a "necessary" entity. To deduce political fatalism from this doctrine is absurd, for the simple reason that historic events are taking place not outside of but through the will of people, through the class struggle if we deal with a class society.
annotation.summary: Historical necessity does not mean passive fatalism; history operates through conscious human agency and the class struggle.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin refutes both bourgeois caricatures of 'fatalist Marxism' and Kautsky's opportunist passivity, showing that recognizing the historical necessity of imperialism guides active revolutionary struggle against it.

annotation.targetText: Hegel's dialectics, which Marx placed on its feet, is valuable for this very reason that it grasps the dialectics of life, that it fearlessly analyses the present without being disturbed by the fact that every existence hides within itself the germ of its own destruction.
annotation.summary: Placed on materialist feet by Marx, dialectics reveals that every historical social form contains the internal contradictions that lead to its overthrow.
annotation.explanation: Contrasting Marx's materialist dialectic with Hegel's mystified idealist form, Bukharin concludes that the sharpening contradictions of finance capitalism inevitably prepare the bursting of the capitalist shell.

annotation.targetText: Our “Left” Communists, however, who are also fond of calling themselves “proletarian” Communists, because there is very little that is proletarian about them and very much that is petty-bourgeois, are incapable of giving thought to the balance of forces, to calculating it. This is the core of Marxism and Marxist tactics, but they disdainfully brush aside the “core” with “proud” phrases
annotation.summary: Calculating the objective material balance of class forces is the core of Marxist tactics, whereas ultra-leftism substitutes subjective phrases for material reality.
annotation.explanation: Lenin exposes the philosophical idealism and petty-bourgeois class character of ultra-leftism: instead of analyzing real material and military conditions, Left Communists treat their own subjective revolutionary desires as sufficient.

annotations.chapterTitle: I. The Brest Peace and the Balance of Forces

annotation.summary: A transitional post-revolutionary economy contains five intermingled socio-economic structures, from peasant small commodity production to state capitalism and socialism.
annotation.explanation: Rather than treating the transitional economy as an abstract binary between pure capitalism and pure socialism, Lenin conducts a concrete materialist analysis of the five coexisting modes of production in Soviet Russia.

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: Socialism is inconceivable without large-scale capitalist engineering based on the latest discoveries of modern science. It is inconceivable without planned state organisation, which keeps tens of millions of people to the strictest observance of a unified standard in production and distribution.
annotation.summary: Socialism requires the material foundation of modern large-scale engineering, scientific technology, and unified state economic planning.
annotation.explanation: Lenin emphasizes that socialism cannot be built on fragmented small-scale production; it requires assimilating the most advanced technological and organizational achievements developed under large-scale capitalism.

annotations.chapterTitle: IV. Large-Scale Engineering and National Accounting

annotation.targetText: On the one hand, it would be a fatal mistake to declare that since there is a discrepancy between our economic “forces” and our political strength, it “follows” that we should not have seized power.[4] Such an argument can be advanced only by a “man in a muffler”,[5] who forgets that there will always be such a “discrepancy”, that it always exists in the development of nature as well as in the development of society, that only by a series of attempts: each of which, taken by itself, will be one sided and will suffer from certain inconsistencies: will complete socialism be created by the revolutionary co-operation of the proletarians of all countries.
annotation.summary: Refusing to seize political power until economic conditions are 'perfect' is mechanical dogmatism; uneven development is universal in nature and history.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes both Menshevik determinism (which claimed Russia was too economically backward for revolution) and ultra-left impatience, showing that proletarian state power can be used to consciously accelerate material development.

annotations.chapterTitle: V. Compromises, Labour Discipline, and Socialist Construction

annotation.targetText: Science demands, first, that the experience of other countries be taken into account, especially if these other countries, which are also capitalist, are undergoing, or have recently undergone, a very similar experience; second, it demands that account be taken of all the forces, groups, parties, classes and masses operating in a given country, and also that policy should not be determined only by the desires and views, by the degree of class-consciousness and the militancy of one group or party alone.
annotation.summary: Revolutionary strategy must be grounded in an objective analysis of all class forces, not the subjective militancy of an ultra-left minority.
annotation.explanation: Lenin contrasts scientific socialism with ultra-left voluntarism, showing that communists cannot base their tactics merely on their own hatred of bourgeois politicians while ignoring where the majority of workers currently stand.

annotation.targetText: The extension of Freudian hypotheses seems 'educated', even scientific, but it is ignorant, bungling. Freudian theory is the modern fashion.
annotation.summary: Lenin critiques bourgeois psychoanalytic fashions that replace materialist class analysis with individualist sexual speculation.
annotation.explanation: Lenin argues that fashionable Freudian pamphlets flourishing in bourgeois society divert working-class activists away from collective struggle into self-absorbed individual psychology.

annotation.targetText: Forms of marriage and of the family, in their historical development and dependence upon economic life, are calculated to destroy the superstition existing in the minds of working women concerning the eternal character of bourgeois society.
annotation.summary: Zetkin demonstrates that studying the historical evolution of the family exposes capitalism as a temporary, changeable system.
annotation.explanation: Drawing on Engels's Origin of the Family, Zetkin points out that when working women learn how family structures change across economic modes of production, they realize bourgeois property relations are not eternal.

annotation.targetText: You must be aware of the famous theory that in communist society the satisfaction of sexual desires, of love, will be as simple and unimportant as drinking a glass of water. This glass of water theory has made our young people mad, quite mad.
annotation.summary: Critique of the "glass of water" theory: reducing love and relationships to mechanical biological urges is vulgar anti-Marxism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin rejects the popular distortion that communism reduces love to a trivial physiological need, noting that such mechanical reductionism ignores culture, mutual respect, and social responsibility.

annotation.targetText:
the determining factor in history
is, in the final instance, the production and reproduction of the immediate
essentials of li
annotation.summary: Human history is fundamentally shaped by two practical activities: producing physical goods to survive (food, tools, shelter) and producing new human beings (childbirth, family, and child-rearing).
annotation.explanation: Human history is fundamentally shaped by two practical activities: producing physical goods to survive (food, tools, shelter) and producing new human beings (childbirth, family, and child-rearing).
annotation.context: Engels lays down the bedrock principle of historical materialism. Social systems, moral codes, and legal structures do not fall from the sky; they are built upon how a society produces material goods and organizes family life.

annotation.context: Before private property developed, human communities were structured around communal kinship bonds. Social obligations were determined by clan relationships rather than state laws or money.

annotation.context: Engels critiques bourgeois ideology for projecting modern capitalist family structures backward into prehistory. In reality, human family systems evolved dramatically across different economic stages.

annotation.explanation: The consanguine (generation-based) family stage is no longer practiced anywhere today, but its historical existence is proven by ancient kinship naming systems preserved in language.
annotation.context: Engels shows how anthropologists deduce prehistoric social stages. Even after actual marriage customs change, old kinship terms linger in language, allowing historians to reconstruct earliest human family forms.

annotation.explanation: As men accumulated private property in livestock and land, they abolished traditional matriarchal inheritance customs so their wealth could pass directly to their biological children.
annotation.context: In early communal clan systems, descent was traced through the mother, and property stayed within the mother's clan line. Private property accumulation created economic pressure to shift to male-line father-right inheritance.

annotation.context: Engels analyzes the economic origins of patriarchal marriage. When individual men accumulated wealth (livestock, land, slaves), they demanded guaranteed paternity so their accumulated private property could pass directly to their biological offspring.

The proof that the kinship organizations
designated by animal names in a tribe of American Indians are essentially
identical with the genea of the Greeks and the gentes of the Romans; that the
American is the original form and the Greek and Roman forms are later and
derivative; that the whole social organization of the primitive Greeks and
Romans into gens, phratry, and tribe finds its faithful parallel in that of the

annotation.summary: The clan (gens) was the universal social structure of human societies before the rise of private property, class distinctions, and state authority.
annotation.explanation: The clan (gens) was the universal social structure of human societies before the rise of private property, class distinctions, and state authority.
annotation.context: Engels highlights Morgan's discovery that early Greek, Roman, Germanic, and Native American societies were all organized around egalitarian kinship clans. These clans managed public affairs democratically without standing armies, police, or kings.

annotation.context: Engels traces the early history of classical Greece. As private property accumulated in individual households, male-line inheritance replaced communal clan inheritance, marking the beginning of class division in Greek society.

The oldest Celtic laws which have been preserved show the gens still fully
alive: in Ireland, after being forcibly broken up by the English, it still
lives today in the consciousness of the people, as an instinct at any rate; in
Scotland it was still in full strength in the middle of the eighteenth century,
and here again it succumbed only to the weapons, laws, and courts of the
English.
annotation.summary: Communal clan organization and shared land tenure survived among Celtic communities in Ireland and Scotland until destroyed by British military force and capitalist property laws.
annotation.explanation: Communal clan organization and shared land tenure survived among Celtic communities in Ireland and Scotland until destroyed by British military force and capitalist property laws.
annotation.context: Engels demonstrates that communal clan structures existed across Western Europe as well. In the Scottish Highlands, tribal clan solidarity resisted state centralization until suppressed following the 18th-century Jacobite uprisings.

annotation.targetText: The state is therefore by no means a power imposed on society from without
annotation.summary: The state is not a neutral mediator above society. It is created when internal class divisions produce conflicts that cannot be peacefully resolved.
annotation.explanation: The state is not a neutral mediator above society. It is created when internal class divisions produce conflicts that cannot be peacefully resolved.
annotation.context: Engels refutes idealist views (such as Hegel's) that claim the state represents ultimate moral reason. The state arises specifically because society splits into hostile economic classes with opposing interests.

annotation.context: Engels presents the Marxist vision of the withering away of the state. Once production is organized cooperatively and class oppression ends, standing police forces and state coercion become obsolete.

annotation.targetText: According to the present conception of the party, trade-union and parliamentary activity are important for the socialist movement because such activity prepares the proletariat, that is to say, creates the subjective factor of the socialist transformation, for the task of realising socialism.
annotation.summary: Creating the subjective factor: trade union and parliamentary action build working-class solidarity and class consciousness necessary for taking power, rather than altering capitalist property relations directly.
annotation.explanation: Creating the subjective factor: trade union and parliamentary action build working-class solidarity and class consciousness necessary for taking power, rather than altering capitalist property relations directly.

annotations.chapterTitle: The Consequences of Social Reformism and General Nature of Reformism

annotation.targetText: The greatest conquest of the developing proletarian movement has been the discovery of grounds of support for the realisation of socialism in the economic condition of capitalist society. As a result of this discovery, socialism was changed from an "ideal" dreamt of by humanity for thousands of years to a thing of historic necessity.
annotation.summary: From Utopian to Scientific Socialism: Marxism proves that socialism is not a moral wish, but an economic necessity arising from the inherent contradictions of capitalist production.
annotation.explanation: From Utopian to Scientific Socialism: Marxism proves that socialism is not a moral wish, but an economic necessity arising from the inherent contradictions of capitalist production.

annotation.targetText: Legislative reform and revolution are not different methods of historic development that can be picked out at the pleasure from the counter of history, just as one chooses hot or cold sausages. Legislative reform and revolution are different factors in the development of class society.
annotation.summary: Luxemburg's iconic rejection of reformist choice: reform and revolution are not menu options for political activists; legislative reform operates within the boundaries of existing class society, whereas revolution creates a new social order.

It is also perfectly obvious that one or the other grouping of the great powers is determined, not by a community of certain racial tasks, but by a community of capitalist aims at a given moment.
annotation.summary: Bukharin demolishes racial theories of imperialism, showing that military alliances follow capitalist profit interests rather than racial identity.
annotation.explanation: Pointing to multi-ethnic war coalitions and shifting alliances among European and Asian powers, Bukharin exposes racial ideology as a ruling-class fabrication designed to mask the war aims of finance capital.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. IX: Imperialism as an Historic Category

annotation.targetText: Marxism teaches us that the historic process, and consequently every link in the chain of historic events, is a "necessary" entity. To deduce political fatalism from this doctrine is absurd, for the simple reason that historic events are taking place not outside of but through the will of people, through the class struggle if we deal with a class society.
annotation.summary: Historical necessity does not mean passive fatalism; history operates through conscious human agency and the class struggle.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin refutes both bourgeois caricatures of 'fatalist Marxism' and Kautsky's opportunist passivity, showing that recognizing the historical necessity of imperialism guides active revolutionary struggle against it.

annotation.targetText: For the collapse of the proletarian movement is a result of the unequal situation of the "state capitalist trusts" within the boundaries of world economy. Just as it is impossible to understand modern capitalism and its imperialist policy without analysing the tendencies of world capitalism, so the basic tendencies in the proletarian movement cannot be understood without analysing world capitalism.
annotation.summary: The 1914 betrayal of the Second International stemmed from the privileged position of imperialist state-capitalist trusts in the world economy.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin shows how superprofits from colonial exploitation allowed metropolitan capitalists to cultivate a reformist labor aristocracy that temporarily identified its interests with its own imperialist state.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XIV: World Economy and Proletarian Socialism

annotation.targetText: To recognise defence of the fatherland means recognising the legitimacy and justice of war. Legitimacy and justice from what point of view? Only from the point of view of the socialist, proletariat and its struggle for its emancipation. We do not recognise any other point of view. If war is waged by the exploiting class with the object of strengthening its rule as a class, such a war is a criminal war, and “defencism” in such a war is a base betrayal of socialism. If war is waged by the proletariat after it has conquered the bourgeoisie in its own country, and is waged with the object of strengthening and developing socialism, such a war is legitimate and “holy”.
annotation.summary: Marxism judges the justice of a war not by abstract moral formulas, but by which class wages it and for what historical aim.
annotation.explanation: While defending a capitalist nation in an imperialist war is a betrayal of the working class, defending a socialist republic where workers have overthrown the bourgeoisie is a legitimate internationalist duty.

annotations.chapterTitle: II. Proletarian Defencism and Revolutionary Phrase-Making

annotation.targetText: It is in the interest of capital to destroy its enemy (the revolutionary proletariat) bit by bit, before the workers in all countries have united (actually united, i.e., by beginning the revolution). It is in our interest to do all that is possible, to take advantage of the slightest opportunity to postpone the decisive battle until the moment (or until after the moment) the revolutionary workers’ contingents have united in a single great international army.
annotation.summary: Strategic retreat and playing for time protect an isolated socialist revolution from being crushed piecemeal by international capital.
annotation.explanation: Lenin shows that genuine proletarian internationalism requires preserving the existing bastion of socialist power until revolutionary movements in other countries mature.

annotation.targetText: The Fascist Party created a double-edged weapon for the corruption and terrorisation of the working class. annotation.targetText: The proletariat must have a well organised apparatus of self-defence. Whenever Fascism uses violence, it must be met with proletarian violence. This struggle can only be successful if there is a proletarian united front. The workers must unite for this struggle regardless of party.
annotation.summary: Defeating fascism requires a Proletarian United Front across party lines and organized armed working-class self-defense.

annotation.targetText:
Although the working-day is not a fixed, but a fluent quantity,
it can, on the other hand, only vary within certain limits. The minimum
limit is, however, not determinable; of course, if we make the extension
line B; ‑C or the surplus-labour = 0, we have a minimum limit, i.e.,
the part of the day which the labourer must necessarily work for his own
maintenance. On the basis of capitalist production, however, this necessary
labour can form a part only of the working-day; the working-day itself
can never be reduced to this minimum. On the other hand, the working-day
has a maximum limit. It cannot be prolonged beyond a certain point. This
maximum limit is conditioned by two things. First, by the physical bounds
of labour-power. Within the 24 hours of the natural day a man can expend
only a definite quantity of his vital force. A horse, in like manner, can
only work from day to day, 8 hours. During part of the day this force must
rest, sleep; during another part the man has to satisfy other physical
needs, to feed, wash, and clothe himself. Besides these purely physical
limitations, the extension of the working-day encounters moral ones. The
labourer needs time for satisfying his intellectual and social wants, the
extent and number of which are conditioned by the general state of social
advancement. The variation of the working-day fluctuates, therefore, within
physical and social bounds. But both these limiting conditions are of a
very elastic nature, and allow the greatest latitude. So we find working-days
of 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 hours, i.e., of the most different lengths.
annotation.summary: The working day has both physical limits (the body needs sleep and food) and moral limits (workers need education, social life, and leisure). Capital constantly pushes against both boundaries.
annotation.explanation: The working day has both physical limits (the body needs sleep and food) and moral limits (workers need education, social life, and leisure). Capital constantly pushes against both boundaries.

annotation.targetText:
A locomotive, for instance, consists of more than 5,000
independent parts. It cannot, however, serve as an example of the first
kind of genuine manufacture, for it is a structure produced by modern mechanical
industry. But a watch can; and William Petty used it to illustrate the
division of labour in manufacture. Formerly the individual work of a Nuremberg
artificer, the watch has been transformed into the social product of an
immense number of detail labourers, such as mainspring makers, dial makers,
spiral spring makers, jewelled hole makers, ruby lever makers, hand makers,
case makers, screw makers, gilders, with numerous subdivisions, such as
wheel makers (brass and steel separate), pin makers, movement makers, acheveur
de pignon (fixes the wheels on the axles, polishes the facets, &c.),
pivot makers, planteur de finissage (puts the wheels and springs in the
works), finisseur de barillet (cuts teeth in the wheels, makes the holes
of the right size, &c.), escapement makers, cylinder makers for cylinder
escapements, escapement wheel makers, balance wheel makers, raquette makers
(apparatus for regulating the watch), the planteur d'échappement
(escapement maker proper); then the repasseur de barillet (finishes the
box for the spring, &c.), steel polishers, wheel polishers, screw polishers,
figure painters, dial enamellers (melt the enamel on the copper), fabricant
de pendants (makes the ring by which the case is hung), finisseur de charnière
(puts the brass hinge in the cover, &c.), faiseur de secret (puts in
the springs that open the case), graveur, ciseleur, polisseur de bo�te,
&c., &c., and last of all the repasseur, who fits together the
whole watch and hands it over in a going state. Only a few parts of the
watch pass through several hands; and all these membra disjecta come together
for the first time in the hand that binds them into one mechanical whole.
This external relation between the finished product, and its various and
diverse elements makes it, as well in this case as in the case of all similar
finished articles, a matter of chance whether the detail labourers are
brought together in one workshop or not. The detail operations may further
be carried on like so many independent handicrafts, as they are in the
Cantons of Vaud and Neufchâtel; while in Geneva there exist large
watch manufactories where the detail labourers directly co-operate under
the control of a single capitalist. And even in the latter case the dial, the springs, and the case, are seldom made in the factory itself. To carry
on the trade as a manufacture, with concentration of workmen, is, in the
watch trade, profitable only under exceptional conditions, because competition
is greater between the labourers who desire to work at home, and because
the splitting up of the work into a number of heterogeneous processes,
permits but little use of the instruments of labour in common, and the
capitalist, by scattering the work, saves the outlay on workshops,
&c. [7] Nevertheless the position of this detail
labourer who, though he works at home, does so for a capitalist (manufacturer,
établisseur), is very different from that of the independent artificer,
who works for his own customers. [8]
annotation.summary: Under manufacture, each worker performs only one tiny fraction of the total production process. This "detail laborer" becomes extremely skilled at their single task but loses the ability to produce a complete product independently.

We have laid bare three fundamental motives for the conquest policies of modern capitalist states: increased competition in the sales markets, in the markets of raw materials, and for the spheres of capital investment. This is what the modern development of capitalism and its transformation into finance capitalism has brought about.

Those three roots of the policy of finance capitalism, however, represent in substance only three facets of the same phenomenon, namely of the conflict between the growth of productive forces on the one hand, and the "national" limits of the production organisation on the other.
annotation.summary: The three drivers of imperialist conquest (sales markets, raw materials, and capital investment spheres) stem from the conflict between global productive forces and national bourgeois states.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin synthesizes his theory of imperialism: productive forces have outgrown the narrow framework of the nation-state, forcing finance capital to attempt to resolve the contradiction through military conquest.

annotation.explanation: Instead of competing merely through lower prices, state-capitalist trusts deploy tariffs, credit blockades, raw material boycotts, and military force to crush foreign rivals.

annotation.summary: Imperialist world war acts as a gigantic crisis that destroys productive forces while vastly accelerating finance-capitalist centralization and state capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin documents how World War I wiped out small enterprises, subordinated entire national economies to state-capitalist war syndicates, and propelled the United States to global financial supremacy.

annotation.summary: A transitional post-revolutionary economy contains five intermingled socio-economic structures, from peasant small commodity production to state capitalism and socialism.

annotation.explanation: Because monopoly capitalism centralizes banking, trusts, and distribution networks on a national scale, replacing the bourgeois state with a proletarian Soviet state turns state-monopoly mechanisms into instruments of socialist construction.

annotations.chapterTitle: IV. Large-Scale Engineering and National Accounting

annotation.targetText: On the one hand, it would be a fatal mistake to declare that since there is a discrepancy between our economic “forces” and our political strength, it “follows” that we should not have seized power.[4] Such an argument can be advanced only by a “man in a muffler”,[5] who forgets that there will always be such a “discrepancy”, that it always exists in the development of nature as well as in the development of society, that only by a series of attempts: each of which, taken by itself, will be one sided and will suffer from certain inconsistencies: will complete socialism be created by the revolutionary co-operation of the proletarians of all countries.
annotation.summary: Refusing to seize political power until economic conditions are 'perfect' is mechanical dogmatism; uneven development is universal in nature and history.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes both Menshevik determinism (which claimed Russia was too economically backward for revolution) and ultra-left impatience, showing that proletarian state power can be used to consciously accelerate material development.

annotation.targetText:
Bukharin noted and emphasised that the old state machinery must be “smashed” and “blown up”, that the bourgeoisie must be “finally and completely strangled” and so on. The frenzied petty bourgeoisie may also want this. And this, in the main, is what our revolution has already done between October 1917 and February 1918.

In my pamphlet I also mention what even the most revolutionary petty bourgeois cannot want, what the class-conscious proletarian does want, what our revolution has not yet accomplished. On this task, the task of tomorrow, Bukharin said nothing.
annotation.summary: While petty-bourgeois revolutionaries focus only on smashing the old order, proletarian revolutionaries must also build disciplined accounting, control, and labor organization.
annotation.explanation: Lenin highlights the decisive boundary between anarchistic or ultra-left destruction and Marxist-Leninist construction: smashing the bourgeois state is only the first step toward building a disciplined socialist economy.

As soon as this process of transformation has sufficiently decomposed
the old society from top to bottom, as soon as the labourers are turned
into proletarians, their means of labour into capital, as soon as the capitalist
mode of production stands on its own feet, then the further socialisation
of labour and further transformation of the land and other means of production
into socially exploited and, therefore, common means of production, as
well as the further expropriation of private proprietors, takes a new form.
That which is now to be expropriated is no longer the labourer working for
himself, but the capitalist exploiting many labourers. This expropriation
is accomplished by the action of the immanent laws of capitalistic production
itself, by the centralisation of capital. One capitalist always kills many.
Hand in hand with this centralisation, or this expropriation of many capitalists
by few, develop, on an ever-extending scale, the cooperative form of the
labour process, the conscious technical application of science, the methodical
cultivation of the soil, the transformation of the instruments of labour
into instruments of labour only usable in common, the economising of all
means of production by their use as means of production of combined, socialised
labour, the entanglement of all peoples in the net of the world market,
and with this, the international character of the capitalistic regime.
Along with the constantly diminishing number of the magnates of capital,
who usurp and monopolise all advantages of this process of transformation,
grows the mass of misery, oppression, slavery, degradation, exploitation;
but with this too grows the revolt of the working class, a class always
increasing in numbers, and disciplined, united, organised by the very mechanism
of the process of capitalist production itself. The monopoly of capital
becomes a fetter upon the mode of production, which has sprung up and flourished
along with, and under it. Centralisation of the means of production and
socialisation of labour at last reach a point where they become incompatible
with their capitalist integument. This integument is burst asunder. The
knell of capitalist private property sounds. The expropriators are expropriated.

annotation.targetText: War in capitalist society is only one of the methods of capitalist competition, when the latter extends to the sphere of world economy. This is why war is an immanent law of a society producing goods under the pressure of the blind laws of a spontaneously developing world market, but it cannot be the law of a society that consciously regulates the process of production and distribution.
annotation.summary: Under capitalism, war is not an accidental breakdown of order, but an immanent law of capitalist competition extended to the world market.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin shows that eliminating free competition inside national borders does not end capitalist anarchy; instead, it projects competition onto the global arena as armed conflict between rival capitalist powers.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. III: Organisation Forms of World Economy

annotation.targetText: Yesterday, the main task of the moment was, as determinedly as possible, to nationalise, confiscate, beat down and crush the bourgeoisie, and put down sabotage. Today, only a blind man could fail to see that we have nationalised, confiscated, beaten down and put down more than we have had time to count. The difference between socialisation and simple confiscation is that confiscation can be carried out by “determination” alone, without the ability to calculate and distribute properly, whereas socialisation cannot be brought about without this ability.
annotation.summary: Confiscation requires only political determination, whereas genuine socialization requires the organizational capacity to calculate, account for, and distribute production.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes the ultra-left illusion that decreeing further nationalizations automatically creates socialism; real socialization demands nationwide accounting, administration, and disciplined economic coordination.

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: It is not state capitalism that is at war with socialism, but the petty bourgeoisie plus private capitalism fighting together against both state capitalism and socialism. The petty bourgeoisie oppose every kind of state interference, accounting and control, whether it be state capitalist or state socialist. This is an absolutely unquestionable fact of reality, and the root of the economic mistake of the “Left Communists” is that they have failed to understand it.
annotation.summary: In a predominantly small-peasant economy, the primary internal threat to socialism is petty-bourgeois profiteering and resistance to state accounting, not state capitalism.
annotation.explanation: By attacking 'state capitalism' in 1918, the Left Communists inadvertently aided small-proprietor grain speculators and private black-marketeers who opposed all state regulation and accounting.

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: Socialism is inconceivable without large-scale capitalist engineering based on the latest discoveries of modern science. It is inconceivable without planned state organisation, which keeps tens of millions of people to the strictest observance of a unified standard in production and distribution.
annotation.summary: Socialism requires the material foundation of modern large-scale engineering, scientific technology, and unified state economic planning.
annotation.explanation: Lenin emphasizes that socialism cannot be built on fragmented small-scale production; it requires assimilating the most advanced technological and organizational achievements developed under large-scale capitalism.

annotation.explanation: Because monopoly capitalism centralizes banking, trusts, and distribution networks on a national scale, replacing the bourgeois state with a proletarian Soviet state turns state-monopoly mechanisms into instruments of socialist construction.

annotation.summary: Socialism is not an idealist figment of the imagination, but the working class's practical appropriation and mastery of large-scale organization created by capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Against the idealist fantasy that socialism can be invented out of pure revolutionary willpower without technical expertise, Lenin insists that the proletarian state must employ and learn from first-class technical specialists under workers' oversight.

 we mean the attitude of the different classes of society

annotation.targetText: Bourgeois scholars and publicists usually come out in defence

annotation.targetText: are justly called "social-imperialists,"

annotations.bookTitle: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism

annotation.targetText: From all that has been said in this book on the economic essence of imperialism, it follows that we must define it as capitalism in transition, or, more precisely, as moribund capitalism.
annotation.summary: Imperialism is decaying, moribund capitalism: the final transitional stage where corporate concentration and socialized production set the stage for a planned socialist economy.
annotation.explanation: Imperialism is decaying, moribund capitalism: the final transitional stage where corporate concentration and socialized production set the stage for a planned socialist economy.
annotation.context: Monopoly capitalism organizes production on a massive, global scale. All that remains is to transfer ownership of these socialized industries from private monopolists to society as a whole.

annotations.bookTitle: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
annotations.chapterTitle: X. The Place of Imperialism in History

annotation.targetText: The most dangerous of all in this respect are those who do not wish to understand that the fight against imperialism is a sham and humbug unless it is inseparably bound up with the fight against opportunism.
annotation.summary: Opposing imperialism is impossible without simultaneously struggling against reformist political leaders who compromise with financial monopolies and defend imperialist wars.
annotation.explanation: Opposing imperialism is impossible without simultaneously struggling against reformist political leaders who compromise with financial monopolies and defend imperialist wars.
annotation.context: Lenin stresses that working-class movements cannot succeed if their leaders accept crumbs from imperial superprofits and support national corporate interests over global solidarity.

annotations.bookTitle: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
annotations.chapterTitle: X. The Place of Imperialism in History

annotation.targetText: The scientific significance of N.I. Bukharin's work consists particularly in this, that he examines the fundamental facts of world economy relating to imperialism as a whole, as a definite stage in the growth of most highly developed capitalism.
annotation.summary: Lenin highlights that imperialism must be analyzed scientifically as a definite historical stage of highly developed monopoly capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Rather than treating imperialism as a reversible diplomatic policy choice or a moral insult, Marxism analyzes it as the necessary economic stage reached when free competition gives way to monopoly.

annotation.targetText: The typical ruler of the world became finance capital, a power that is peculiarly mobile and flexible, peculiarly intertwined at home and internationally, peculiarly devoid of individuality and divorced from the immediate processes of production, peculiarly easy to concentrate, a power that has already made peculiarly large strides on the road of concentration, so that literally several hundred billionaires and millionaires hold in their hands the fate of the whole world.
annotation.summary: Finance capital concentrates global economic and political power into the hands of a few hundred financial oligarchs.
annotation.explanation: Lenin describes how the fusion of banking and industrial capital creates a hyper-mobile financial oligarchy divorced from direct production yet commanding the fate of nations.

annotation.targetText: There is no doubt that the development is going in the direction of a single world trust that will swallow up all enterprises and all states without exception. But the development in this direction is proceeding under such stress, with such a tempo, with such contradictions, conflicts, and convulsions-not only economical, but also political, national, etc., etc.-that before a single world trust will be reached, before the respective national finance capitals will have formed a world union of "ultra-imperialism," imperialism will inevitably explode, capitalism will turn into its opposite.
annotation.summary: Before global capitalism could ever unite into Kautsky's peaceful 'single world trust', its violent contradictions will cause imperialism to explode in socialist revolution.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes Karl Kautsky's reformist dream of 'ultra-imperialism', demonstrating that the uneven, catastrophic development of monopoly capitalism intensifies wars and class struggles long before a global monopoly could peacefully consolidate.

annotation.targetText: It is the most ardent wish of the author that this book should soon be transformed from a weapon against imperialism into an historic document relegated to the archives.
annotation.summary: Written as a theoretical weapon against world imperialism, Bukharin looks forward to the complete overthrow of capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Writing immediately after the Bolshevik seizure of power in November 1917, Bukharin connects theoretical economic analysis directly to the practical revolutionary struggle to abolish imperialism.

annotation.targetText: The cleavage between "town and country," as well as the "development of this cleavage," formerly confined to one country only, are now being reproduced on a tremendously enlarged basis. Viewed from this standpoint, entire countries appear to-day as "towns," namely, the industrial countries, whereas entire agrarian territories appear to be "country."
annotation.summary: World capitalism reproduces the division between town and country on a global scale, turning industrial powers into 'towns' and agrarian colonies into 'country'.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin extends Marx's analysis of the urban-rural division of labor to the world economy, explaining how uneven capitalist development polarizes the globe into industrial manufacturing centers and dependent agricultural or extractive peripheries.

annotation.targetText: International connections may grow in scope, spreading over territories not yet drawn into the vortex of capitalist life. In that case we speak of the extensive growth of world economy. On the other hand, they may assume greater depth, become more frequent, forming, as it were, a thicker net-work. In that case we have an intensive growth of world economy.
annotation.summary: The world economy expands both extensively (through colonial annexation of non-capitalist lands) and intensively (through deeper global production ties).
annotation.explanation: Bukharin distinguishes the two dimensions of capitalist globalization: geographical expansion into precapitalist territories and the deepening interdependence of global industry, transport, and finance.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. II: Growth of World Economy

annotation.targetText: War in capitalist society is only one of the methods of capitalist competition, when the latter extends to the sphere of world economy. This is why war is an immanent law of a society producing goods under the pressure of the blind laws of a spontaneously developing world market, but it cannot be the law of a society that consciously regulates the process of production and distribution.
annotation.summary: Under capitalism, war is not an accidental breakdown of order, but an immanent law of capitalist competition extended to the world market.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin shows that eliminating free competition inside national borders does not end capitalist anarchy; instead, it projects competition onto the global arena as armed conflict between rival capitalist powers.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. III: Organisation Forms of World Economy

annotation.targetText: The conditions of direct exploitation and those of the realisation of surplus value are not identical. They are separated logically as well as by time and space. The first are only limited by the productive power of society, the last by the proportional relations of the various lines of production and by the consuming power of society.
annotation.summary: Quoting Marx's Capital Vol. 3, Bukharin explains how depressed working-class consumption forces monopolies to seek foreign sales markets.
annotation.explanation: Because capitalism restricts the purchasing power of the domestic working masses while expanding mass production, monopolies are driven to dump surplus commodities abroad and annex colonial markets.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. V: World Sales Markets and Changed Sales Conditions

annotation.targetText: We have in mind the disproportion between the development of industry and the development of agriculture as a source of raw material for the manufacturing industry.
annotation.summary: The lagging development of agriculture behind rapid industrial growth triggers a global scramble among monopolies to seize raw material sources.
annotation.explanation: Because monopoly ownership of land holds back agricultural output while manufacturing demand for cotton, rubber, timber, and ores skyrockets, imperialist powers fight to monopolize colonial raw material supplies.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. VI: World Market for Raw Materials, and Change in the Conditions of Purchasing Materials

annotation.targetText: For monopoly organisations can overcome the tendency towards lowering the rate of profit by receiving monopoly superprofits at the expense of the non-trustified industries. Out of the surplus value created every year, one portion, that which has been created in the nontrustified branches of industry, is being transferred to the coowners of capitalist monopolies, whereas the share of the outsiders continually decreases. Thus the entire process drives capital beyond the frontiers of the country.
annotation.summary: Cartels and trusts restrict domestic investment to maintain monopoly superprofits, driving overaccumulated capital to seek higher returns abroad.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin explains the economic compulsion behind capital export: monopoly cartels limit domestic output to keep prices high and export their surplus capital to colonies and foreign markets.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. VII: World Movement of Capital, and Change in the Economic Forms of International Connections

annotation.targetText:
We have laid bare three fundamental motives for the conquest policies of modern capitalist states: increased competition in the sales markets, in the markets of raw materials, and for the spheres of capital investment. This is what the modern development of capitalism and its transformation into finance capitalism has brought about.

Those three roots of the policy of finance capitalism, however, represent in substance only three facets of the same phenomenon, namely of the conflict between the growth of productive forces on the one hand, and the "national" limits of the production organisation on the other.
annotation.summary: The three drivers of imperialist conquest (sales markets, raw materials, and capital investment spheres) stem from the conflict between global productive forces and national bourgeois states.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin synthesizes his theory of imperialism: productive forces have outgrown the narrow framework of the nation-state, forcing finance capital to attempt to resolve the contradiction through military conquest.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. VIII: World Economy and the "National" State

annotation.targetText: It is perfectly obvious that not races but state organisations of definite groups of the bourgeoisie are conducting the struggle. It is also perfectly obvious that one or the other grouping of the great powers is determined, not by a community of certain racial tasks, but by a community of capitalist aims at a given moment.
annotation.summary: Bukharin demolishes racial theories of imperialism, showing that military alliances follow capitalist profit interests rather than racial identity.
annotation.explanation: Pointing to multi-ethnic war coalitions and shifting alliances among European and Asian powers, Bukharin exposes racial ideology as a ruling-class fabrication designed to mask the war aims of finance capital.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. IX: Imperialism as an Historic Category

annotation.targetText: By concentration we understand the increase of capital that is due to the capitalisation of the surplus value produced by that capital; under centralisation we understand the joining together of various individual capital units which thus form a new larger unit.
annotation.summary: Concentration grows capital through reinvesting surplus value, while centralization merges existing capitals into giant trusts and state-capitalist blocs.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin applies Marx's laws of concentration and centralization to the world economy, showing how national economies coalesce into competing 'state-capitalist trusts' that wage war to centralize territory.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. X: Reproduction of the Process of Concentration and Centralisation on a World Scale

annotation.targetText: The growth of competition outlined in the last chapter reduces itself to the fact that the continuous elimination of competition among smaller economic units calls forth a sharper competition among large economic units.
annotation.summary: Eliminating competition among small firms inside a nation intensifies destructive competition among giant state-capitalist trusts on the world stage.
annotation.explanation: Instead of competing merely through lower prices, state-capitalist trusts deploy tariffs, credit blockades, raw material boycotts, and military force to crush foreign rivals.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XI: Means of Competitive Struggle, and State Power

annotation.targetText: Marxism teaches us that the historic process, and consequently every link in the chain of historic events, is a "necessary" entity. To deduce political fatalism from this doctrine is absurd, for the simple reason that historic events are taking place not outside of but through the will of people, through the class struggle if we deal with a class society.
annotation.summary: Historical necessity does not mean passive fatalism; history operates through conscious human agency and the class struggle.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin refutes both bourgeois caricatures of 'fatalist Marxism' and Kautsky's opportunist passivity, showing that recognizing the historical necessity of imperialism guides active revolutionary struggle against it.

annotation.targetText: Together with a truly barbarous squandering of production forces, with the destruction of the material means of production and of the living labour power, together with the devitalisation of economy through monstrous socially harmful expenditures, the war, like a gigantic crisis, has intensified the fundamental tendencies of capitalist development; it has hastened to an extraordinary degree the growth of finance capitalist relations and the centralisation of capital on a world scale.
annotation.summary: Imperialist world war acts as a gigantic crisis that destroys productive forces while vastly accelerating finance-capitalist centralization and state capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin documents how World War I wiped out small enterprises, subordinated entire national economies to state-capitalist war syndicates, and propelled the United States to global financial supremacy.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XIII: War and Economic Evolution

annotation.targetText: For the collapse of the proletarian movement is a result of the unequal situation of the "state capitalist trusts" within the boundaries of world economy. Just as it is impossible to understand modern capitalism and its imperialist policy without analysing the tendencies of world capitalism, so the basic tendencies in the proletarian movement cannot be understood without analysing world capitalism.
annotation.summary: The 1914 betrayal of the Second International stemmed from the privileged position of imperialist state-capitalist trusts in the world economy.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin shows how superprofits from colonial exploitation allowed metropolitan capitalists to cultivate a reformist labor aristocracy that temporarily identified its interests with its own imperialist state.

annotations.chapterTitle: Ch. XIV: World Economy and Proletarian Socialism

annotation.targetText: For, until the world socialist revolution breaks out, until it embraces several countries and is strong enough to overcome international imperialism, it is the direct duty of the socialists who have conquered in one country (especially a backward one) not to accept battle against the giants of imperialism. Their duty is to try to avoid battle, to wait until the conflicts between the imperialists weaken them even more, and bring the revolution in other countries even nearer.
annotation.summary: A newly victorious socialist state encircled by stronger imperialist powers must avoid premature military battle and utilize inter-imperialist contradictions.
annotation.explanation: Defending the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk against the Left Communists, Lenin shows that preserving the revolutionary state requires sober material calculation rather than walking into a military trap set by stronger imperialist powers.

annotations.chapterTitle: I. The Brest Peace and the Balance of Forces

annotation.targetText: For our “Lefts” merely brandish a cardboard sword when they ignore the universally known fact, of which the war in the Ukraine has served as an additional proof, that peoples utterly exhausted by three years of butchery cannot go on fighting without a respite; and that war, if it cannot be organised on a national scale, very often creates a mentality of disintegration peculiar to petty proprietors, instead of the iron discipline of the proletariat.
annotation.summary: Ignoring the material exhaustion of the masses to demand immediate 'revolutionary war' is brandishing a cardboard sword.
annotation.explanation: Lenin contrasts proletarian discipline grounded in the real material conditions of working people with the aristocratic idealism of petty-bourgeois intellectuals who despise the war-weary masses' need for a breathing space.

annotations.chapterTitle: I. The Brest Peace and the Balance of Forces

annotation.targetText: To recognise defence of the fatherland means recognising the legitimacy and justice of war. Legitimacy and justice from what point of view? Only from the point of view of the socialist, proletariat and its struggle for its emancipation. We do not recognise any other point of view. If war is waged by the exploiting class with the object of strengthening its rule as a class, such a war is a criminal war, and “defencism” in such a war is a base betrayal of socialism. If war is waged by the proletariat after it has conquered the bourgeoisie in its own country, and is waged with the object of strengthening and developing socialism, such a war is legitimate and “holy”.
annotation.summary: Marxism judges the justice of a war not by abstract moral formulas, but by which class wages it and for what historical aim.
annotation.explanation: While defending a capitalist nation in an imperialist war is a betrayal of the working class, defending a socialist republic where workers have overthrown the bourgeoisie is a legitimate internationalist duty.

annotations.chapterTitle: II. Proletarian Defencism and Revolutionary Phrase-Making

annotation.targetText: It is a universal revolution and will, accordingly, have a universal theater.
annotation.summary: Because capitalist production is global, socialist transformation requires international working-class cooperation and anti-imperialist solidarity.
annotation.explanation: Because capitalist production is global, socialist transformation requires international working-class cooperation and anti-imperialist solidarity.

annotations.chapterTitle: 19. Will It Be Possible for This Revolution to Take Place in One Country Alone?

annotation.targetText: The nationalities of the peoples associating themselves in accordance with the principle of community will be compelled to mingle with each other as a result of this association
annotation.summary: International economic integration and shared social interests render national chauvinism and imperialist borders historically obsolete.
annotation.explanation: International economic integration and shared social interests render national chauvinism and imperialist borders historically obsolete.

annotations.chapterTitle: 22. What Will Be the Attitude of Communism to Existing Nationalities?

annotation.targetText: When Vassilissa met a detachment on the street, going to war in full military array, she always had to turn away.
annotation.summary: Vassilissa's early Bolshevik consciousness rejects imperialist war and capitalist slaughter in favor of working-class internationalism.
annotation.explanation: Vassilissa's early Bolshevik consciousness rejects imperialist war and capitalist slaughter in favor of working-class internationalism.

annotation.targetText: The Third International is, in contradistinction to the old International, an International of all races without any distinctions whatever.
annotation.summary: Zetkin affirms that the Communist International unites working people of all races without any racial hierarchy or colonial chauvinism.
annotation.explanation: Contrasting the Comintern with the European-chauvinist Second International (which tolerated colonialism), Zetkin emphasizes that revolutionary communism is built on uncompromising racial equality and global anti-imperialist solidarity.

annotation.targetText: We must create a powerful international women's movement, on a clear theoretical basis
annotation.summary: Lenin insists that women's liberation requires an international mass movement grounded in scientific socialist theory.
annotation.explanation: Rather than leaving women's organization to bourgeois charities or spontaneous reformism, Lenin argues the Communist International must build a theoretically rigorous movement of working women.

annotation.targetText: There is no good practice without Marxist theory, that is clear. The greatest clarity of principle is necessary for us communists in this question. There must be a sharp distinction between ourselves and all other Parties.
annotation.summary: Revolutionary practice depends on theoretical clarity that separates communist women's liberation from bourgeois feminism and reformism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin stresses that communists must draw a clear class line between proletarian women's emancipation (which requires abolishing private property in the means of production) and bourgeois feminism.

annotation.targetText: In Petrograd, here in Moscow, in other towns and industrial centres the women workers acted splendidly during the revolution. Without them we should not have been victorious.
annotation.summary: Working-class women were indispensable to the victory and defense of the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution.
annotation.explanation: Lenin highlights that proletarian women in Russia bore extreme material deprivation and fought on the front lines of the revolution, proving their central role in working-class victory.

annotation.targetText: The first proletarian dictatorship is a real pioneer in establishing social equality for women. It is clearing away more prejudices than could volumes of feminist literature.
annotation.summary: Workers' power achieves concrete material and legal equality for women far beyond bourgeois feminist rhetoric.
annotation.explanation: By overthrowing capitalist property relations and placing working women in Soviet governance and public administration, the workers' state dismantled centuries of legal and social subordination.

annotation.targetText: They are, unfortunately, doubly sacrificed by bourgeois society. First, by its accursed property system, and, secondly, by its accursed moral hypocrisy.
annotation.summary: Capitalism forces impoverished women into prostitution through economic destitution and then hypocritically criminalizes them.
annotation.explanation: Following Rosa Luxemburg's materialist critique, Lenin notes that bourgeois society drives working-class women into prostitution through poverty while subjecting them to police persecution and moral condemnation.

annotation.targetText: Take them back to productive work, bring them into the social economy. That is what we must do.
annotation.summary: The socialist solution to prostitution is economic reintegration into dignified, productive social labor.
annotation.explanation: Consistent with Soviet policy later detailed by Alexandra Kollontai, Lenin argues that ending prostitution requires eliminating women's economic destitution and bringing women into collective production.

annotation.targetText: The extension of Freudian hypotheses seems 'educated', even scientific, but it is ignorant, bungling. Freudian theory is the modern fashion.
annotation.summary: Lenin critiques bourgeois psychoanalytic fashions that replace materialist class analysis with individualist sexual speculation.
annotation.explanation: Lenin argues that fashionable Freudian pamphlets flourishing in bourgeois society divert working-class activists away from collective struggle into self-absorbed individual psychology.

annotation.targetText: The great social question appears as an adjunct, a part, of sexual problems. The main thing becomes a subsidiary matter. That not only endangers clarity on that question itself, it muddles the thoughts, the class-consciousness of proletarian women generally.
annotation.summary: Treating class struggle as secondary to personal sexual theories confuses working-class consciousness.
annotation.explanation: Lenin warns that isolating sex and marriage from the struggle against capitalist exploitation inverts Marxist priorities and weakens revolutionary focus during acute political crises.

annotation.targetText: The decay, the corruption, the filth of bourgeois marriage, with its difficult divorce, its freedom for the man, its enslavement for the woman, the repulsive hypocrisy of sexual morality and relations fill the most active minded and best people with deep disgust.
annotation.summary: Bourgeois marriage traps women in legal and economic servitude while excusing male privilege and double standards.
annotation.explanation: Lenin condemns capitalist marriage laws that sanctify private property, restrict divorce, and enforce female subordination behind a facade of moral respectability.

annotation.targetText: You must be aware of the famous theory that in communist society the satisfaction of sexual desires, of love, will be as simple and unimportant as drinking a glass of water. This glass of water theory has made our young people mad, quite mad.
annotation.summary: Critique of the "glass of water" theory: reducing love and relationships to mechanical biological urges is vulgar anti-Marxism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin rejects the popular distortion that communism reduces love to a trivial physiological need, noting that such mechanical reductionism ignores culture, mutual respect, and social responsibility.

annotation.targetText: Drinking water is, of course, an individual affair. But in love two lives are concerned, and a third, a new life, arises, it is that which gives it its social interest, which gives rise to a duty towards the community.
annotation.summary: Human love is fundamentally social rather than purely individual because it involves mutual lives and the community.
annotation.explanation: Unlike an isolated physical act, romantic and family relationships affect another person and potentially children, creating ethical and social responsibilities within a socialist collective.

annotation.targetText: Communism will not bring asceticism, but joy of life, power of life, and a satisfied love life will help to do that.
annotation.summary: Communist morality rejects religious asceticism and celebrates a healthy, fulfilled, and joyful human life.
annotation.explanation: Lenin clarifies that critiquing bourgeois promiscuity has nothing in common with monastic self-denial; socialism aims to free love from economic coercion so people can live full, joyful lives.

annotation.targetText: The thesis must clearly point out that real freedom for women is possible only through communism. The inseparable connection between the social and human position of the woman, and private property in the means of production, must be strongly brought out. That will draw a clear and ineradicable line of distinction between our policy and feminism.
annotation.summary: True women's liberation requires abolishing private ownership of the means of production, distinguishing Marxism from bourgeois feminism.
annotation.explanation: While bourgeois feminism seeks equal rights within the existing capitalist hierarchy, Marxism proves that women's oppression is structurally rooted in private property and class exploitation.

annotation.targetText: No special organisations for women. A woman communist is a member of the Party just as a man communist, with equal rights and duties. There can be no difference of opinion on that score. Nevertheless, we must not close our eyes to the fact that the Party must have bodies, working groups, commissions, committees, bureaus or whatever you like, whose particular duty it is to arouse the masses of women workers
annotation.summary: Equal membership in a single Communist Party combined with specialized Party women's commissions for mass agitation.
annotation.explanation: Lenin balances organizational unity (men and women fighting together in one vanguard party) with practical revolutionary reality (dedicated women's bureaus like the Soviet Zhenotdel to organize working women).

annotation.targetText: The rejection of the necessity for separate bodies for our work among the women masses is a conception allied to those of our highly principled and most radical friends of the Communist Labour Party. According to them there must be only one form of organisation, workers' unions. I know them. Many revolutionary but confused minds appeal to principle 'whenever ideas are lacking'.
annotation.summary: Lenin critiques the ultra-left Communist Labour Party for appealing to abstract 'pure principle' to reject practical organizational work among women.

annotation.targetText: Unless millions of women are with us we cannot exercise the proletarian dictatorship, cannot construct on communist lines. We must find our way to them, we must study and try to find that way.

annotation.targetText: Our demands are practical conclusions which we have drawn from the burning needs, the shameful humiliation of women, in bourgeois society, defenceless and without rights.

annotation.targetText: Unfortunately it is still true to say of many of our comrades, 'scratch a communist and find a philistine'. 0f course, you must scratch the sensitive spot, their mentality as regards women. annotation.targetText: Our communist work among the women, our political work, embraces a great deal of educational work among men. We must root out the old 'master' idea to its last and smallest root, in the Party and among the masses.
annotation.summary: Women's emancipation requires systematic ideological struggle to uproot patriarchal "master" privilege among working-class men.
annotation.explanation: Lenin insists that communist work on the woman question is never just "women's work": the Party must actively re-educate male workers to abandon domestic privilege and treat women as equal comrades.

annotation.targetText: We are establishing communal kitchens and public eating-houses, laundries and repairing shops, nurseries, kindergartens, children's homes, educational institutes of all kinds. annotation.explanation: Legal equality on paper is insufficient if women remain chained to unpaid domestic labor; Soviet power builds collective public infrastructure so women can develop their full human and political capacities.

annotation.targetText: For every day of the existence of the Soviet State proves more clearly that we cannot go forward without the women.
annotation.summary: The progress and survival of socialist society depend directly on the full participation and leadership of emancipated women.
annotation.explanation: Lenin concludes that building a new socialist order requires millions of working women actively shaping economic production, public administration, and cultural life.
