annotation.summary: Strategic retreat and playing for time protect an isolated socialist revolution from being crushed piecemeal by international capital.
annotation.explanation: Lenin shows that genuine proletarian internationalism requires preserving the existing bastion of socialist power until revolutionary movements in other countries mature.

annotations.chapterTitle: II. Proletarian Defencism and Revolutionary Phrase-Making

annotation.targetText: Yesterday, the main task of the moment was, as determinedly as possible, to nationalise, confiscate, beat down and crush the bourgeoisie, and put down sabotage. Today, only a blind man could fail to see that we have nationalised, confiscated, beaten down and put down more than we have had time to count. The difference between socialisation and simple confiscation is that confiscation can be carried out by “determination” alone, without the ability to calculate and distribute properly, whereas socialisation cannot be brought about without this ability.
annotation.summary: Confiscation requires only political determination, whereas genuine socialization requires the organizational capacity to calculate, account for, and distribute production.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes the ultra-left illusion that decreeing further nationalizations automatically creates socialism; real socialization demands nationwide accounting, administration, and disciplined economic coordination.

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: It is not state capitalism that is at war with socialism, but the petty bourgeoisie plus private capitalism fighting together against both state capitalism and socialism. The petty bourgeoisie oppose every kind of state interference, accounting and control, whether it be state capitalist or state socialist. This is an absolutely unquestionable fact of reality, and the root of the economic mistake of the “Left Communists” is that they have failed to understand it.
annotation.summary: In a predominantly small-peasant economy, the primary internal threat to socialism is petty-bourgeois profiteering and resistance to state accounting, not state capitalism.
annotation.explanation: By attacking 'state capitalism' in 1918, the Left Communists inadvertently aided small-proprietor grain speculators and private black-marketeers who opposed all state regulation and accounting.

annotations.chapterTitle: III. State Capitalism and the Transition to Socialism

annotation.targetText: At present, petty-bourgeois capitalism prevails in Russia, and it is one and the same road that leads from it to both large-scale state capitalism and to socialism, through one and the same intermediary station called “national accounting and control of production and distribution”. Those who fail to understand this are committing an unpardonable mistake in economics. Either they do not know the facts of life, do not see what actually exists and are unable to look the truth in the face, or they confine themselves to abstractly comparing “capitalism” with “socialism” and fail to study the concrete forms and stages of the transition that is taking place in our country.
annotation.summary: Abstractly counterposing 'capitalism' and 'socialism' ignores the concrete material intermediary stages required to transition from small-scale production to socialism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin critiques the idealist method of the Left Communists, who compare abstract concepts of capitalism and socialism in their heads instead of studying the real material pathway of national accounting and control.

annotation.targetText:
As soon as this process of transformation has sufficiently decomposed
the old society from top to bottom, as soon as the labourers are turned
into proletarians, their means of labour into capital, as soon as the capitalist
mode of production stands on its own feet, then the further socialisation
of labour and further transformation of the land and other means of production
into socially exploited and, therefore, common means of production, as
well as the further expropriation of private proprietors, takes a new form.
That which is now to be expropriated is no longer the labourer working for
himself, but the capitalist exploiting many labourers. This expropriation
is accomplished by the action of the immanent laws of capitalistic production
itself, by the centralisation of capital. One capitalist always kills many.
Hand in hand with this centralisation, or this expropriation of many capitalists
by few, develop, on an ever-extending scale, the cooperative form of the
labour process, the conscious technical application of science, the methodical
cultivation of the soil, the transformation of the instruments of labour
into instruments of labour only usable in common, the economising of all
means of production by their use as means of production of combined, socialised
labour, the entanglement of all peoples in the net of the world market,
and with this, the international character of the capitalistic regime.
Along with the constantly diminishing number of the magnates of capital,
who usurp and monopolise all advantages of this process of transformation,
grows the mass of misery, oppression, slavery, degradation, exploitation;
but with this too grows the revolt of the working class, a class always
increasing in numbers, and disciplined, united, organised by the very mechanism
of the process of capitalist production itself. The monopoly of capital
becomes a fetter upon the mode of production, which has sprung up and flourished
along with, and under it. Centralisation of the means of production and
socialisation of labour at last reach a point where they become incompatible
with their capitalist integument. This integument is burst asunder. The
knell of capitalist private property sounds. The expropriators are expropriated.
annotation.summary: Capitalist accumulation leads to extreme centralization and socialized production. Eventually, the monopoly of capital becomes a fetter, leading to the socialist transformation.
annotation.explanation: Capitalist accumulation leads to extreme centralization and socialized production. Eventually, the monopoly of capital becomes a fetter, leading to the socialist transformation.

The analysis of landed property in its various historical forms is beyond
the scope of this work. We shall be concerned with it only in so far as a
portion of the surplus-value produced by capital falls to the share of the
landowner. We assume, then, that agriculture is dominated by the capitalist
mode of production just as manufacture is; in other words, that agriculture is
carried on by capitalists who differ from other capitalists primarily in the
manner in which their capital, and the wage-labour set in motion by this
capital, are invested. So far as we are concerned, the farmer produces wheat,
etc., in much the same way as the manufacturer produces yarn or machines. The
assumption that the capitalist mode of production has encompassed agriculture
implies that it rules over all spheres of production and bourgeois society,
i.e., that its prerequisites, such as free competition among capitals, the
possibility of transferring the latter from one production sphere to another,
and a uniform level of the average profit, etc., are fully matured. The form of
landed property which we shall consider here is a specifically historical one a
form transformed through the influence of capital and of the
capitalist mode of production, either of feudal landownership, or of
small-peasant agriculture as a means of livelihood, in which the
possession of the land and the soil constitutes one of the
prerequisites of production for the direct producer, and in which his
ownership of land appears as the most advantageous condition for the
prosperity of his mode of production. Just as the capitalist mode of
production in general is based on the expropriation of the conditions of labour
from the labourers, so does it in agriculture presuppose the expropriation of
the rural labourers from the land and their subordination to a capitalist, who
carries on agriculture for the sake of profit. Thus, for the purpose of our
analysis, the objection that other forms of landed property and of agriculture
have existed, or still exist, is quite irrelevant. Such an objection can only
apply to those economists who treat the capitalist mode of production in
agriculture, and the form of landed property corresponding to it, not as
historical but rather as eternal categories.
annotation.summary: Ground rent is the share of surplus value that flows to landowners simply because they hold legal monopoly over land. The capitalist farmer extracts surplus value from workers, then surrenders part of it to the landowner as rent.
annotation.explanation: Ground rent is the share of surplus value that flows to landowners simply because they hold legal monopoly over land. The capitalist farmer extracts surplus value from workers, then surrenders part of it to the landowner as rent.

As soon as this process of transformation has sufficiently decomposed
the old society from top to bottom, as soon as the labourers are turned
into proletarians, their means of labour into capital, as soon as the capitalist
mode of production stands on its own feet, then the further socialisation
of labour and further transformation of the land and other means of production
into socially exploited and, therefore, common means of production, as
well as the further expropriation of private proprietors, takes a new form.
That which is now to be expropriated is no longer the labourer working for
himself, but the capitalist exploiting many labourers. This expropriation
is accomplished by the action of the immanent laws of capitalistic production
itself, by the centralisation of capital. One capitalist always kills many.
Hand in hand with this centralisation, or this expropriation of many capitalists
by few, develop, on an ever-extending scale, the cooperative form of the
labour process, the conscious technical application of science, the methodical
cultivation of the soil, the transformation of the instruments of labour
into instruments of labour only usable in common, the economising of all
means of production by their use as means of production of combined, socialised
labour, the entanglement of all peoples in the net of the world market,
and with this, the international character of the capitalistic regime.
Along with the constantly diminishing number of the magnates of capital,
who usurp and monopolise all advantages of this process of transformation,
grows the mass of misery, oppression, slavery, degradation, exploitation;
but with this too grows the revolt of the working class, a class always
increasing in numbers, and disciplined, united, organised by the very mechanism
of the process of capitalist production itself. The monopoly of capital
becomes a fetter upon the mode of production, which has sprung up and flourished
along with, and under it. Centralisation of the means of production and
socialisation of labour at last reach a point where they become incompatible
with their capitalist integument. This integument is burst asunder. The
knell of capitalist private property sounds. The expropriators are expropriated.

annotation.targetText: A commodity appears, at first sight, a very trivial thing, and easily understood. Its analysis shows that it is, in reality, a very queer thing, abounding in metaphysical subtleties and theological niceties. So far as it is a value in use, there is nothing mysterious about it, whether we consider it from the point of view that by its properties it is capable of satisfying human wants, or from the point that those properties are the product of human labour. It is as clear as noon-day, that man, by his industry, changes the forms of the materials furnished by Nature, in such a way as to make them useful to him. The form of wood, for instance, is altered, by making a table out of it. Yet, for all that, the table continues to be that common, every-day thing, wood. But, so soon as it steps forth as a commodity, it is changed into something transcendent. It not only stands with its feet on the ground, but, in relation to all other commodities, it stands on its head, and evolves out of its wooden brain grotesque ideas, far more wonderful than "table-turning" ever was. [26a]

annotation.targetText: There is no doubt that the development is going in the direction of a single world trust that will swallow up all enterprises and all states without exception. annotation.targetText: Marxism teaches us that the historic process, and consequently every link in the chain of historic events, is a "necessary" entity. annotation.targetText: For the collapse of the proletarian movement is a result of the unequal situation of the "state capitalist trusts" within the boundaries of world economy. annotation.summary: The 1914 betrayal of the Second International stemmed from the privileged position of imperialist state-capitalist trusts in the world economy.

annotation.targetText: Bernstein began his revision of the Social-Democracy by abandoning the theory of capitalist collapse. The latter, however, is the corner-stone of scientific socialism.

annotation.explanation: The 1891 Erfurt Programme of German Social-Democracy demanded that 'religion is a private matter.' Lenin clarifies Engels's distinction: while the workers' party demands that the bourgeois state treat religion as a private matter (disestablishing state churches, ending clerical subsidies, and guaranteeing freedom of conscience), the party itself must never treat religion as a private matter, but must actively champion dialectical materialism and educate workers against religious ideology.

annotation.targetText: For, until the world socialist revolution breaks out, until it embraces several countries and is strong enough to overcome international imperialism, it is the direct duty of the socialists who have conquered in one country (especially a backward one) not to accept battle against the giants of imperialism. annotation.summary: A newly victorious socialist state encircled by stronger imperialist powers must avoid premature military battle and utilize inter-imperialist contradictions.

annotation.targetText: On the one hand, it would be a fatal mistake to declare that since there is a discrepancy between our economic “forces” and our political strength, it “follows” that we should not have seized power.[4] Such an argument can be advanced only by a “man in a muffler”,[5] who forgets that there will always be such a “discrepancy”, that it always exists in the development of nature as well as in the development of society, that only by a series of attempts: each of which, taken by itself, will be one sided and will suffer from certain inconsistencies: will complete socialism be created by the revolutionary co-operation of the proletarians of all countries.
annotation.summary: Refusing to seize political power until economic conditions are 'perfect' is mechanical dogmatism; uneven development is universal in nature and history.
annotation.explanation: Lenin refutes both Menshevik determinism (which claimed Russia was too economically backward for revolution) and ultra-left impatience, showing that proletarian state power can be used to consciously accelerate material development.

annotation.targetText:
“The German Communists are Communists because, through all the intermediate stations and all compromises created, not by them but by the course of historical development, they clearly perceive and constantly pursue the final aim; the abolition of classes and the creation of a society in which there will no longer be private ownership of land or of the means of production. The thirty-three Blanquists are Communists just because they imagine that, merely because they want to skip the intermediate stations and compromises, the matter is settled, and if ‘it begins’ in the next few days; which they take for granted; and they take over power, ‘communism will be introduced’ the day after tomorrow. If that is not immediately possible, they are not Communists.

“What childish innocence it is to present one’s own impatience as a theoretically convincing argument!”
annotation.summary: Engels and Lenin critique Blanquist ultra-leftism for mistaking revolutionary impatience for Marxist strategy.

annotation.targetText: Science demands, first, that the experience of other countries be taken into account, especially if these other countries, which are also capitalist, are undergoing, or have recently undergone, a very similar experience; second, it demands that account be taken of all the forces, groups, parties, classes and masses operating in a given country, and also that policy should not be determined only by the desires and views, by the degree of class-consciousness and the militancy of one group or party alone.
annotation.summary: Revolutionary strategy must be grounded in an objective analysis of all class forces, not the subjective militancy of an ultra-left minority.
annotation.explanation: Lenin contrasts scientific socialism with ultra-left voluntarism, showing that communists cannot base their tactics merely on their own hatred of bourgeois politicians while ignoring where the majority of workers currently stand.

annotation.targetText: “The Communist Party must not compromise. . . . The Communist Party must keep its doctrine pure, and its independence of reformism inviolate, its mission is to lead the way, without stopping or turning, by the direct road to the communist revolution.”
annotation.summary: Ultra-leftism treats doctrinal purity as a substitute for winning over the working-class majority through practical political experience.
annotation.explanation: Distinguishing between necessary tactical compromises that preserve organizational strength vs. opportunist surrenders of principle is essential for political leadership.

annotation.targetText: To act otherwise would mean hampering the cause of the revolution, since revolution is impossible without a change in the views of the majority of the working class, a change brought about by the political experience of the masses, never by propaganda alone.
annotation.summary: The working masses cannot be won to revolution by propaganda alone; they must learn through their own practical political experience.
annotation.explanation: Lenin explains why ultra-left abstentionism fails: when a small revolutionary minority refuses to engage with mass organizations or elections, it abandons the masses instead of helping them see through reformist leaders in practice.

annotation.summary: Immediate struggles must bridge working women's daily grievances to the necessity of working-class political power.
annotation.explanation: Abstract slogans alone cannot mobilize unorganized women; communists must link concrete economic and social demands to the goal of establishing a workers' state that guarantees full equality.

annotation.targetText: In all probability, the proletarian revolution will transform existing society gradually and will be able to abolish private property only when the means of production are available in sufficient quantity.

The Fascist leaders are not a small and exclusive caste; they extend deeply into wide elements of the population.

annotation.targetText: The Communist Parties must not only be the vanguard of the proletarian manual workers, but also the energetic defenders of the interests of the brain workers. annotation.targetText: The proletariat must have a well organised apparatus of self-defence. Whenever Fascism uses violence, it must be met with proletarian violence. I do not mean by this individual terrorist acts, but the violence of the organised revolutionary class struggle of the proletariat. Germany has made a beginning by organising factory "hundreds." This struggle can only be successful if there is a proletarian united front. The workers must unite for this struggle regardless of party.

We have laid bare three fundamental motives for the conquest policies of modern capitalist states: increased competition in the sales markets, in the markets of raw materials, and for the spheres of capital investment. This is what the modern development of capitalism and its transformation into finance capitalism has brought about.

Those three roots of the policy of finance capitalism, however, represent in substance only three facets of the same phenomenon, namely of the conflict between the growth of productive forces on the one hand, and the "national" limits of the production organisation on the other.
annotation.summary: The three drivers of imperialist conquest (sales markets, raw materials, and capital investment spheres) stem from the conflict between global productive forces and national bourgeois states.
annotation.explanation: Bukharin synthesizes his theory of imperialism: productive forces have outgrown the narrow framework of the nation-state, forcing finance capital to attempt to resolve the contradiction through military conquest.

annotation.targetText: It is perfectly obvious that not races but state organisations of definite groups of the bourgeoisie are conducting the struggle. annotation.summary: Bukharin demolishes racial theories of imperialism, showing that military alliances follow capitalist profit interests rather than racial identity.
annotation.explanation: Pointing to multi-ethnic war coalitions and shifting alliances among European and Asian powers, Bukharin exposes racial ideology as a ruling-class fabrication designed to mask the war aims of finance capital.

annotation.summary: Lenin insists that women's liberation requires an international mass movement grounded in scientific socialist theory.
annotation.explanation: Rather than leaving women's organization to bourgeois charities or spontaneous reformism, Lenin argues the Communist International must build a theoretically rigorous movement of working women.

annotation.targetText: The question of reform or revolution, of the final goal and the movement, is basically, in another form, but the question of the petty-bourgeois or proletarian character of the labour movement.
annotation.summary: Identifying the class nature of revisionism: Bernstein's reformist slogan ('the movement is everything, the final goal nothing') reflects a petty-bourgeois desire to settle comfortably within capitalism rather than a proletarian struggle for emancipation.
annotation.explanation: Identifying the class nature of revisionism: Bernstein's reformist slogan ('the movement is everything, the final goal nothing') reflects a petty-bourgeois desire to settle comfortably within capitalism rather than a proletarian struggle for emancipation.

annotation.targetText: The latter must not direct its daily activity toward the conquest of political power, but toward the betterment of the condition of the working class, within the existing order. It must not expect to institute socialism as a result of a political and social crisis, but should build socialism by means of the progressive extension of social control and the gradual application of the principle of co-operation.
annotation.summary: Summarizing Bernstein's opportunist method: revisionism abandons the conquest of political power, proposing instead to manage capitalism through gradual legislative and cooperative reforms.
annotation.explanation: Summarizing Bernstein's opportunist method: revisionism abandons the conquest of political power, proposing instead to manage capitalism through gradual legislative and cooperative reforms.

annotation.targetText: That is why people who pronounce themselves in favour of the method of legislative reform in place and in contradistinction to the conquest of political power and social revolution, do not really choose a more tranquil, calmer and slower road to the same goal, but a different goal. Instead of taking a stand for the establishment of a new society they take a stand for surface modifications of the old society.
annotation.summary: Exposing revisionism's true objective: substituting reform for revolution does not reach socialism slowly—it abandons socialism altogether in favor of managing and preserving capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Exposing revisionism's true objective: substituting reform for revolution does not reach socialism slowly—it abandons socialism altogether in favor of managing and preserving capitalism.

annotation.targetText: What appears to characterise this practice above all? A certain hostility to "theory." This is quite natural, for our "theory," that is, the principles of scientific socialism, impose clearly marked limitations to practical activity : insofar as it concerns the aims of this activity, the means used in attaining these aims and the method employed in this activity.
annotation.summary: Why revisionism shuns theory: opportunist politics prioritizes immediate short-term compromises over long-term strategic analysis, fearing that rigorous theory will expose its abandonment of revolutionary goals.
annotation.explanation: Why revisionism shuns theory: opportunist politics prioritizes immediate short-term compromises over long-term strategic analysis, fearing that rigorous theory will expose its abandonment of revolutionary goals.

annotation.targetText: For some the statement "socialism is a religion" is a form of transition from religion to socialism; for others, it is a form of transition from socialism to religion
annotation.summary: Evaluating religious terminology in agitation: distinguishing naive popular metaphors from revisionist 'god-building'.
annotation.explanation: Lenin makes a nuanced distinction: when an uneducated worker says 'socialism is my religion', it represents a naive step toward socialist consciousness. However, when intellectuals like Lunacharsky preach 'god-building socialism', it represents an opportunistic retreat into religious revisionism requiring firm party critique.

annotation.targetText: The second root of Fascism lies in the retarding of the world revolution by the treacherous attitude of the reformist leaders. Large numbers of the petty bourgeoisie, including even the middle classes, had discarded their war-time psychology for a certain sympathy with reformist socialism, hoping that the latter would bring about a reformation of society along democratic lines. They were disappointed in their hopes.
annotation.summary: Social-democratic betrayal of socialist revolution drives ruined middle strata and disillusioned workers into the arms of fascism.
annotation.explanation: When reformist leaders collaborate with the bourgeoisie instead of overthrowing capitalism, impoverished petty-bourgeois layers and demoralized workers lose faith in socialism and seek refuge in fascist demagogy.

annotation.targetText: a party becomes stronger by purging itself
annotation.summary: Quoting Ferdinand Lassalle's letter to Marx, Lenin emphasizes that political strength and clarity come from maintaining firm principles rather than compromising with reformists for fake unity.
annotation.explanation: Quoting Ferdinand Lassalle's letter to Marx, Lenin emphasizes that political strength and clarity come from maintaining firm principles rather than compromising with reformists for fake unity.
annotation.context: Lenin argues that a movement cannot build real revolutionary strength by compromising on core principles with reformist factions that dilute its ultimate goals.

annotation.targetText: Social-Democracy must change from a party of social revolution into a democratic party of social reforms.
annotation.summary: Lenin summarizes Bernstein's revisionist demand: abandoning the goal of systemic revolution in favor of piecemeal reforms within the capitalist system.
annotation.explanation: Lenin summarizes Bernstein's revisionist demand: abandoning the goal of systemic revolution in favor of piecemeal reforms within the capitalist system.
annotation.context: Bernsteinian opportunism sought to transform working-class political parties into moderate reform groups that work within existing capitalist institutions.

annotation.targetText: Louis Bonaparte took the political power from the capitalists under the pretext of protecting them
annotation.summary: Bonapartism: state executive power claiming independence while safeguarding capitalist exploitation.
annotation.explanation: Engels analyzes how Bonapartism arises when class struggle produces an equilibrium of weakness: the autocratic state appears to rule above classes while expanding capitalist industry and financial speculation.

annotation.targetText: Fascism is the concentrated expression of the general offensive undertaken by the world bourgeoisie against the proletariat. Its overthrow is therefore an absolute necessity, nay, it is even a question of the every-day existence and of the bread and butter of every ordinary worker.
annotation.summary: Fascism is the concentrated offensive of big capital against the working class and its daily survival.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin establishes that fascism is not an isolated political aberration, but the generalized offensive of the capitalist ruling class to crush working-class living standards and organizations.

annotation.targetText: Fascism, on the contrary, viewed objectively, is not the revenge of the bourgeoisie in retaliation for proletarian aggression against the bourgeoisie, but it is a punishment of the proletariat for failing to carry on the revolution begun in Russia. The Fascist leaders are not a small and exclusive caste; they extend deeply into wide elements of the population.
annotation.summary: Unlike a narrow military junta, fascism is a mass movement that punishes the working class for an uncompleted socialist revolution.
annotation.explanation: Contrasting Mussolini's movement with Admiral Horthy's officer clique in Hungary, Zetkin explains that fascism builds a broad social base among displaced layers of society when reformist betrayal stalls proletarian revolution.

annotation.targetText: Fascism, with all its forcefulness in the prosecution of its violent deeds, is indeed nothing else but the expression of the disintegration and decay of capitalist economy, and the symptom of the dissolution of the bourgeois State.
annotation.summary: Fascist violence is not a sign of capitalist vitality, but a symptom of capitalist economic decay and state crisis.
annotation.explanation: Where social-democratic reformists cowered before the supposed invulnerability of the bourgeoisie, Zetkin shows that the ruling class turns to fascism precisely because normal parliamentary institutions and capitalist economics are breaking down.

annotation.targetText: The second root of Fascism lies in the retarding of the world revolution by the treacherous attitude of the reformist leaders. Large numbers of the petty bourgeoisie, including even the middle classes, had discarded their war-time psychology for a certain sympathy with reformist socialism, hoping that the latter would bring about a reformation of society along democratic lines. They were disappointed in their hopes.
annotation.summary: Social-democratic betrayal of socialist revolution drives ruined middle strata and disillusioned workers into the arms of fascism.
annotation.explanation: When reformist leaders collaborate with the bourgeoisie instead of overthrowing capitalism, impoverished petty-bourgeois layers and demoralized workers lose faith in socialism and seek refuge in fascist demagogy.

annotation.targetText: Fascism has diverse characteristics in different countries. Nevertheless it has two distinguishing features in all countries, namely, the pretence of a revolutionary programme, which is cleverly adapted to the interests and demands of the large masses, and, on the other hand, the application of the most brutal violence.
annotation.summary: The dual weapon of fascism everywhere: pseudo-revolutionary anti-capitalist demagogy combined with brutal anti-worker terror.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin identifies the universal formula of fascism: it wins mass support by mimicking anti-elitist, revolutionary slogans appealing to ruined lower classes, while deploying paramilitary terror squads against organized labor.

annotation.targetText: The Fascist Party created a double-edged weapon for the corruption and terrorisation of the working class. For the corruption of the working class the Fascist Trade Unions were created, the so-called corporations in which workers and employers were united. To terrorise the working class, the Fascist Party created the militant squads which had grown out of the punitive expeditions.
annotation.summary: Fascist corporatism corrupts labor through class-collaborationist unions while Blackshirt squads terrorize independent workers.
annotation.explanation: In Italy, Mussolini paired Yellow "corporations" (uniting bosses and workers to suppress strikes) with armed paramilitary squads funded by industrialists and landlords to smash revolutionary unions.

annotation.targetText: The destruction of the trade unions has enabled the employers to effect wage reductions of 20 to 30 per cent, and in some cases of even 50 to 60 per cent.
annotation.summary: Once in power, fascism immediately abandons its social promises and enforces massive wage cuts and privatization for big capital.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin documents Mussolini's actual economic record in office: dismantling the eight-hour day, outlawing factory councils, slashing wages by up to 60 percent, abolishing luxury and capital taxes on the rich, and raising indirect taxes on workers.

annotation.targetText: The Third International is, in contradistinction to the old International, an International of all races without any distinctions whatever.
annotation.summary: Zetkin affirms that the Communist International unites working people of all races without any racial hierarchy or colonial chauvinism.
annotation.explanation: Contrasting the Comintern with the European-chauvinist Second International (which tolerated colonialism), Zetkin emphasizes that revolutionary communism is built on uncompromising racial equality and global anti-imperialist solidarity.

annotation.targetText: The Communist Parties must not only be the vanguard of the proletarian manual workers, but also the energetic defenders of the interests of the brain workers. They must be the leaders of all sections of society which are driven into opposition to bourgeois domination because of their interests and their expectations of the future.
annotation.summary: To defeat fascism ideologically, Communist Parties must lead manual workers, intellectual workers, and small peasants alike.
annotation.explanation: Zetkin argues that communists cannot allow fascism to monopolize ruined intellectuals, civil servants, and small peasants; the Party must champion all strata crushed by monopoly capital under the banner of a Workers' and Peasants' Government.

annotation.targetText: The proletariat must have a well organised apparatus of self-defence. Whenever Fascism uses violence, it must be met with proletarian violence. I do not mean by this individual terrorist acts, but the violence of the organised revolutionary class struggle of the proletariat. Germany has made a beginning by organising factory "hundreds." This struggle can only be successful if there is a proletarian united front. The workers must unite for this struggle regardless of party.
annotation.summary: Defeating fascism requires a Proletarian United Front across party lines and organized armed working-class self-defense.
annotation.explanation: Rejecting both passive parliamentary appeals and isolated individual terrorism, Zetkin calls for an all-worker United Front and organized workplace defense squads (factory "hundreds") to crush fascist paramilitaries and overthrow capitalism.

annotation.targetText:
A locomotive, for instance, consists of more than 5,000
independent parts. It cannot, however, serve as an example of the first
kind of genuine manufacture, for it is a structure produced by modern mechanical
industry. But a watch can; and William Petty used it to illustrate the
division of labour in manufacture. Formerly the individual work of a Nuremberg
artificer, the watch has been transformed into the social product of an
immense number of detail labourers, such as mainspring makers, dial makers,
spiral spring makers, jewelled hole makers, ruby lever makers, hand makers,
case makers, screw makers, gilders, with numerous subdivisions, such as
wheel makers (brass and steel separate), pin makers, movement makers, acheveur
de pignon (fixes the wheels on the axles, polishes the facets, &c.),
pivot makers, planteur de finissage (puts the wheels and springs in the
works), finisseur de barillet (cuts teeth in the wheels, makes the holes
of the right size, &c.), escapement makers, cylinder makers for cylinder
escapements, escapement wheel makers, balance wheel makers, raquette makers
(apparatus for regulating the watch), the planteur d'échappement
(escapement maker proper); then the repasseur de barillet (finishes the
box for the spring, &c.), steel polishers, wheel polishers, screw polishers,
figure painters, dial enamellers (melt the enamel on the copper), fabricant
de pendants (makes the ring by which the case is hung), finisseur de charnière
(puts the brass hinge in the cover, &c.), faiseur de secret (puts in
the springs that open the case), graveur, ciseleur, polisseur de bo�te,
&c., &c., and last of all the repasseur, who fits together the
whole watch and hands it over in a going state. Only a few parts of the
watch pass through several hands; and all these membra disjecta come together
for the first time in the hand that binds them into one mechanical whole.
This external relation between the finished product, and its various and
diverse elements makes it, as well in this case as in the case of all similar
finished articles, a matter of chance whether the detail labourers are
brought together in one workshop or not. The detail operations may further
be carried on like so many independent handicrafts, as they are in the
Cantons of Vaud and Neufchâtel; while in Geneva there exist large
watch manufactories where the detail labourers directly co-operate under
the control of a single capitalist. And even in the latter case the dial, the springs, and the case, are seldom made in the factory itself. To carry
on the trade as a manufacture, with concentration of workmen, is, in the
watch trade, profitable only under exceptional conditions, because competition
is greater between the labourers who desire to work at home, and because
the splitting up of the work into a number of heterogeneous processes,
permits but little use of the instruments of labour in common, and the
capitalist, by scattering the work, saves the outlay on workshops,
&c. [7] Nevertheless the position of this detail
labourer who, though he works at home, does so for a capitalist (manufacturer,
établisseur), is very different from that of the independent artificer,
who works for his own customers. [8]
annotation.summary: Under manufacture, each worker performs only one tiny fraction of the total production process. This "detail laborer" becomes extremely skilled at their single task but loses the ability to produce a complete product independently.

annotation.targetText: There is no good practice without Marxist theory, that is clear. The greatest clarity of principle is necessary for us communists in this question. There must be a sharp distinction between ourselves and all other Parties.
annotation.summary: Revolutionary practice depends on theoretical clarity that separates communist women's liberation from bourgeois feminism and reformism.
annotation.explanation: Lenin stresses that communists must draw a clear class line between proletarian women's emancipation (which requires abolishing private property in the means of production) and bourgeois feminism.

annotation.targetText: Communism will not bring asceticism, but joy of life, power of life, and a satisfied love life will help to do that.
annotation.summary: Communist morality rejects religious asceticism and celebrates a healthy, fulfilled, and joyful human life.
annotation.explanation: Lenin clarifies that critiquing bourgeois promiscuity has nothing in common with monastic self-denial; socialism aims to free love from economic coercion so people can live full, joyful lives.

annotation.targetText: According to the present conception of the party, trade-union and parliamentary activity are important for the socialist movement because such activity prepares the proletariat, that is to say, creates the subjective factor of the socialist transformation, for the task of realising socialism.
annotation.summary: Creating the subjective factor: trade union and parliamentary action build working-class solidarity and class consciousness necessary for taking power, rather than altering capitalist property relations directly.
annotation.explanation: Creating the subjective factor: trade union and parliamentary action build working-class solidarity and class consciousness necessary for taking power, rather than altering capitalist property relations directly.

annotations.chapterTitle: The Consequences of Social Reformism and General Nature of Reformism

annotation.targetText: The greatest conquest of the developing proletarian movement has been the discovery of grounds of support for the realisation of socialism in the economic condition of capitalist society. As a result of this discovery, socialism was changed from an "ideal" dreamt of by humanity for thousands of years to a thing of historic necessity.
annotation.summary: From Utopian to Scientific Socialism: Marxism proves that socialism is not a moral wish, but an economic necessity arising from the inherent contradictions of capitalist production.
annotation.explanation: From Utopian to Scientific Socialism: Marxism proves that socialism is not a moral wish, but an economic necessity arising from the inherent contradictions of capitalist production.

annotation.targetText: What appears to characterise this practice above all? A certain hostility to "theory." This is quite natural, for our "theory," that is, the principles of scientific socialism, impose clearly marked limitations to practical activity : insofar as it concerns the aims of this activity, the means used in attaining these aims and the method employed in this activity.
annotation.summary: Why revisionism shuns theory: opportunist politics prioritizes immediate short-term compromises over long-term strategic analysis, fearing that rigorous theory will expose its abandonment of revolutionary goals.
annotation.explanation: Why revisionism shuns theory: opportunist politics prioritizes immediate short-term compromises over long-term strategic analysis, fearing that rigorous theory will expose its abandonment of revolutionary goals.

annotation.targetText: The latter must not direct its daily activity toward the conquest of political power, but toward the betterment of the condition of the working class, within the existing order. It must not expect to institute socialism as a result of a political and social crisis, but should build socialism by means of the progressive extension of social control and the gradual application of the principle of co-operation.
annotation.summary: Summarizing Bernstein's opportunist method: revisionism abandons the conquest of political power, proposing instead to manage capitalism through gradual legislative and cooperative reforms.
annotation.explanation: Summarizing Bernstein's opportunist method: revisionism abandons the conquest of political power, proposing instead to manage capitalism through gradual legislative and cooperative reforms.

annotation.targetText: That is why people who pronounce themselves in favour of the method of legislative reform in place and in contradistinction to the conquest of political power and social revolution, do not really choose a more tranquil, calmer and slower road to the same goal, but a different goal. Instead of taking a stand for the establishment of a new society they take a stand for surface modifications of the old society.
annotation.summary: Exposing revisionism's true objective: substituting reform for revolution does not reach socialism slowly—it abandons socialism altogether in favor of managing and preserving capitalism.
annotation.explanation: Exposing revisionism's true objective: substituting reform for revolution does not reach socialism slowly—it abandons socialism altogether in favor of managing and preserving capitalism.

annotation.targetText: Bernstein began his revision of the Social-Democracy by abandoning the theory of capitalist collapse. The latter, however, is the corner-stone of scientific socialism.
annotation.summary: The cornerstone of scientific socialism: abandoning the analysis of capitalism's collapse forces opportunists to abandon every other element of Marxist theory, leading to total reconciliation with bourgeois society.
annotation.explanation: The cornerstone of scientific socialism: abandoning the analysis of capitalism's collapse forces opportunists to abandon every other element of Marxist theory, leading to total reconciliation with bourgeois society.

annotation.targetText: We still live and think under the heavy hand of an unavoidable loneliness of spirit. Man experiences this "loneliness" even in towns full of noise and people.
annotation.summary: Capitalist atomization generates profound spiritual loneliness, isolating individuals within competitive urban environments.
annotation.explanation: Capitalist atomization generates profound spiritual loneliness, isolating individuals within competitive urban environments.

annotations.bookTitle: Sexual Relations and the Class Struggle
annotations.chapterTitle: 2. The Psychology of Bourgeois Individualism & Loneliness

annotation.targetText: The "potential for loving" of people today is at a low ebb. Men and women seek each other in the hope of finding for themselves, through another person, a means to a larger share of pleasure. They give little thought to what's happening to their partner's emotional and psychological processes.
annotation.summary: How capitalism atomizes emotional life: crude bourgeois individualism reduces personal relationships to transactional self-gratification, draining human capacity for genuine empathy.
annotation.explanation: How capitalism atomizes emotional life: crude bourgeois individualism reduces personal relationships to transactional self-gratification, draining human capacity for genuine empathy.

annotation.targetText: We see that credit, instead of being an instrument for the suppression or the attenuation of crises, is on the contrary a particularly mighty instrument for the formation of crises.
annotation.summary: Refuting the myth that modern financial credit eliminates economic downturns: credit expands production beyond market capacity, delaying crisis only to make the eventual financial collapse far more severe.
annotation.explanation: Refuting the myth that modern financial credit eliminates economic downturns: credit expands production beyond market capacity, delaying crisis only to make the eventual financial collapse far more severe.

annotation.targetText: Co-operatives : especially co-operatives in the field of production constitute a hybrid form in the midst of capitalism. They can be described as small units of socialised production within capitalist exchange.
annotation.summary: The limits of worker co-operatives: producer co-ops operating within a capitalist market are forced to self-exploit their own worker-owners to survive against private corporate competition.
annotation.explanation: The limits of worker co-operatives: producer co-ops operating within a capitalist market are forced to self-exploit their own worker-owners to survive against private corporate competition.

annotation.targetText: When Vassilissa met a detachment on the street, going to war in full military array, she always had to turn away.
annotation.summary: Vassilissa's early Bolshevik consciousness rejects imperialist war and capitalist slaughter in favor of working-class internationalism.
annotation.explanation: Vassilissa's early Bolshevik consciousness rejects imperialist war and capitalist slaughter in favor of working-class internationalism.

annotation.targetText: The present State is, first of all, an organisation of the ruling class. It assumes functions favouring social developments specifically because, and in the measure that, these interests and social developments coincide, in a general fashion, with the interests of the dominant class.
annotation.summary: The class nature of the capitalist state: the state apparatus is fundamentally an instrument of bourgeois class domination, adopting public welfare reforms only when forced by mass pressure or when required to maintain corporate stability.
